configs.default.yaml:
# Master configuration. Every run saves the config it used next to its outputs
# (Tech Spec Section 9.2). Sections are added task by task.
seed: 0

raster:                # input images of the CNN evaluator (Tech Spec 4.2)
  canvas: 8.0          # (spec) meters per side of the fixed canvas; the room sits at its origin
  pixels: 128          # (spec) pixels per side, so 0.0625 m per pixel
  front_strip: 0.10    # (T07) thickness of the band marking an item's front, about 1.6 pixels

generator:             # Set A layouts and the G0 reference (T11, Tech Spec 2.4). Room sizes and
                       # the spacing ranges between items come from rules.yaml.
  attempts: 20         # (T11) placements tried per room; a room that fails them all is dropped
  wall_gap: 0.05       # (T11) an item placed against a wall stands 0 to 5 cm from it
  jitter: 0.05         # (spec) sigma of the position jitter (m)
  walkway: 0.75        # (T11) style (b): clear floor behind the floating sofa, above the 0.6 m
                       # path width so the walkway counts as passable whatever the grid alignment
  armchair_gap: [0.4, 0.9]  # (T11) armchair to the end of the coffee table (the relation allows 1.2)
  shelf_clearance: 0.6 # (T11) clear floor kept in front of the bookshelf
  optional_items:      # (T11) each optional item is in the room with a probability that rises
    area: [10.5, 30.0] # linearly with floor area (m^2) between these two points
    probability: [0.25, 0.75]

set_b:                 # labelled layouts for the CNN evaluator (T13, Tech Spec 2.4). Half are
                       # generator layouts as they come; the other half are perturbed copies,
                       # a tenth of Set B per type: jitter, rotation, random, overlap, near-miss.
  clean_share: 0.5     # (spec)
  jitter_sigmas: [0.1, 0.3, 0.6]  # (spec) m; each sigma gets a third of the jitter share
  jitter_items: 0.5    # (T13) chance that each item is jittered; at least one always is
  near_miss_area: [0.002, 0.0125]  # (T13) overlap of two items, log-uniform, so half fall below
                       # the 0.005 m^2 tolerance (the spec's 0.002-0.05 would make at least 70% invalid)
  near_miss_gap: 0.03  # (T13) door near-miss: from this far clear of the zone to this far inside
  near_miss_reach: 1.0 # (T13) near-miss moves of at most this length (m) are preferred

splits:                # (T14, Tech Spec 2.4)
  fractions: [0.70, 0.15, 0.15]  # (spec) train, validation, test, split by layout
  held_out:            # (spec) rooms that training never sees; Set A and Set B redraw them
    interpolation: {area: [22.0, 26.0]}       # a gap inside the training ranges
    unseen_combination: {area: [32.0, .inf]}  # each W and D occurs in training, not together
    out_of_range: {width: [7.0, 8.0], depth: [6.0, 7.0]}  # beyond the training ranges
  held_out_rooms: 1000 # (T14) rooms per held-out set, each with one generator layout
  diversity_rooms: 200 # (spec) test rooms for the diversity reference (G0) ...
  diversity_layouts: 20  # (spec) ... with this many generator layouts each

dataset:               # the dataset build (T15): python run.py data writes data/<version>/
  version: v1
  set_a: 30000         # (spec, start) good layouts for the CVAE
  set_b: 60000         # (spec, start) labelled layouts for the evaluator
  calibration_rooms: 5000  # (T15) rooms for calibrating f_max, spread evenly over the footprint
                       # ratio (crowded rooms are rare in plain draws)
  calibration_items: 0.5   # (T15) each optional item is in a calibration room with this chance,
                       # whatever the room's size

baselines:             # (T12, Tech Spec 4.3)
  b2_bins: 3           # (T12) B2 groups training rooms into this many width bins and depth bins,
                       # each holding an equal share of the training rooms
  b2_min_examples: 20  # (T12) a bin with fewer examples of an item borrows from rooms of every
                       # size with the same door wall, then from all rooms
  b2_noise: 0.02       # (T12) sigma of the noise added to a drawn u and v
  b2_redraws: 10       # (T12) times an item is drawn again while it overlaps one already placed
  b2_redraw_outside: true   # (T12, chosen after T15) also draw again while the item sticks out of the
                       # room; without it B2 fails mostly because positions taken as fractions of a
                       # larger training room stick out of a smaller one (20% vs 60% raw valid)

evaluation:            # (T16, Tech Spec 6 and 7) the same rooms and samples for every method
  rooms: 500           # (T16) Set A test rooms: the diversity-reference rooms, then random ones
  samples: 64          # (spec) raw samples per room (N = 64 in the pipeline)

cvae:                  # the generator (T19, Tech Spec 4.1); the Week 2 experiments sweep these
  latent: 16           # (spec, start) size of z; E5 tries 4, 16 and 32
  hidden: 256          # (spec) units per hidden layer
  depth: 2             # (spec) hidden layers in the encoder and in the decoder; E3b also tries 6
  activation: relu     # (spec) relu, leaky_relu, elu, gelu, tanh or sigmoid; E3a decides
  batch_norm: true     # (spec) E3b and E6 switch it off
  dropout: 0.1         # (spec) E6 tries 0, 0.1 and 0.3
  position_head: sigmoid  # (spec) sigmoid, or linear (clamped to [0, 1] only when decoding); E7
  position_loss: mse   # (spec) mse, mae or huber; E2
  huber_delta: 0.05    # (spec) E2 tries 0.01, 0.05 and 0.1
  lambda_rot: 1.0      # (spec, start) weight of the rotation cross-entropy
  lambda_overlap: 0.0  # (spec) optional penetration-depth term on decoded positions; E2 and E5
  overlap_margin: 0.0  # (T19) margin of that term: 0, because training layouts may touch

evaluator:             # the CNN evaluator (T20, Tech Spec 4.2)
  channels: [16, 32, 64, 64]  # (spec) the four Conv-BN-ReLU-MaxPool blocks
  hidden: 128          # (spec) units of the dense layer
  dropout: 0.3         # (spec)
  lambda_score: 1.0    # (spec, start) weight of the score regression next to the BCE
  score_loss: mse      # (spec) mse or huber
  huber_delta: 0.1     # (T20) for score_loss huber
  pos_weight: null     # (T20) BCE weight of the valid class; null leaves it unweighted (62% valid)
  batch: 256           # (spec, start)
  lr: 1.0e-3           # (T20, start) Adam

cvae_training:         # (T21, Tech Spec 4.1) python run.py train-cvae
  optimizer: adam      # (spec) adam, sgd, sgd_momentum or rmsprop; E4 compares them
  lr: 1.0e-3           # (spec, start)
  momentum: 0.9        # (spec) for sgd_momentum
  weight_decay: 0.0    # (spec)
  batch: 256           # (spec)
  max_epochs: 200      # (spec)
  beta_target: 0.1     # (spec, start) E5 tries 0.01, 0.1, 0.5 and 1.0
  anneal_epochs: 20    # (spec, start) beta rises linearly from 0 to beta_target over these epochs
  patience: 15         # (spec) epochs without a better validation loss before stopping,
                       # counted only after annealing
  early_stopping: true # (spec) E6 compares it with training for max_epochs
  check_rooms: 100     # (T21) after training, Set A test rooms to sample (64 each) for a first
                       # RVR of M1; the E1 numbers come later, on the frozen configuration
  outliers: 0.0        # (T26) E2's outlier variant: share of the training layouts that get one item
                       # moved to a random spot in the room (0.04 in E2); validation and test stay clean

latent_opt:            # M2: optimize z with the decoder frozen (T23, Tech Spec 5.2)
  steps: 150           # (spec, start) T; E8 tries 0, 25, 50, 100 and 200
  lr: 0.05             # (spec, start) Adam
  lambda_overlap: 10.0 # (spec, start) sum over pairs of the squared penetration depth
  lambda_room: 10.0    # (spec, start) protrusion out of the room
  lambda_door: 10.0    # (spec, start) squared penetration into the door clearance zone
  lambda_pin: 20.0     # (spec, start) squared distance of pinned items from their pins
  lambda_anchor: 0.05  # (spec, start) 0.5 ||z - z0||^2, the anchor to each candidate's start
  lambda_surrogate: 0.0  # (spec) the CNN score term of M3 (P1); 0 for M2
  margin: 0.05         # (spec, start) clearance margin mu of the penetration depths (m)
  tolerance: 1.0e-4    # (T23) a candidate stops once its constraint terms (the anchor not
                       # counted, since it grows whenever z moves) fall below this

pipeline:              # (T25, Tech Spec 5.1 and 5.3)
  candidates: 64       # (spec) N latent samples per request
  latent_opt: true     # (spec) M2; false gives M1
  top_k: 3             # (spec)
  tau_div: 0.3         # (spec, start) a pick must differ from every earlier pick by this much (m)
  relax: 0.25          # (spec) when fewer than top_k qualify, tau_div shrinks by this share ...
  relax_times: 2       # (spec) ... up to this many times
configs.rules.yaml:
# Layout rules and thresholds (Tech Spec Sections 1, 2.2 and 3).
#
# Every number here is our own design assumption, not an official standard (PRD A7), and
# must be presented as one in the report and the viva. Values taken from the Tech Spec are
# marked (spec); values chosen in task T04 are marked (T04). "start" means a starting point
# to be tuned. Lengths are in meters, areas in m^2.

door:
  width: 0.9                 # (spec)
  clearance_depth: 0.9       # (spec) how far the clearance zone reaches into the room
  corner_margin: 0.65        # (spec) m_d: the door centre stays this far from a corner
                             # (half the door width plus 0.2 m)

hard_checks:
  in_room_tol: 1.0e-3        # (spec) H1: a footprint may stick out of the room by this much
  max_pair_overlap: 0.005    # (spec, start) H2: largest allowed intersection of two footprints
  door_overlap_tol: 1.0e-4   # (spec) H3: largest allowed intersection with the clearance zone

reachability:                # H4 (Tech Spec 3.3)
  cell: 0.10                 # (spec) grid cell size. Cells are sampled at their centres, so a
                             # corridor narrower than min_path_width always fails, one at least
                             # min_path_width + cell wide always passes, and one in between
                             # depends on how it lines up with the grid.
  min_path_width: 0.6        # (spec) a walkable cell is at least half of this from obstacles
  access_offset: 0.35        # (spec) the access line runs this far in front of the front face
  access_tolerance: 0.3      # (spec) an item counts as reached if a reached cell is this close
                             # to its access line (the whole face, not just its middle: T08)

feasibility:                 # pre-check (Tech Spec 3.5)
  f_max: 0.38                # (T15) calibrated on data/v1: the generator furnishes half of the rooms
                             # at a footprint ratio of 0.377 (logistic fit, 3,903 rooms). The spec's
                             # starting value was 0.45

quality:                     # soft quality score S (Tech Spec 3.4)
  weights: {align: 0.30, relations: 0.30, circulation: 0.25, space: 0.15}  # (spec)
  wall_distance: 0.10        # (spec) "against a wall" means within this distance of it
  space_band: [0.15, 0.40]   # (spec) best range of furniture area / room area
  space_falloff: 0.15        # (T09) the space score falls linearly to 0 this far outside the
                             # band, so it is 0 for an empty room and at 55% coverage
  relation_falloff: 0.5      # (T09) a relation scores 1 inside its range and falls linearly to
                             # 0 this far outside it; a relation whose items are not all
                             # present is skipped

rooms:
  living_room:
    width: [3.5, 7.0]        # (spec) sampling range of W
    depth: [3.0, 6.0]        # (spec) sampling range of D
    against_wall: [tv_unit, bookshelf]  # (T04) back to a wall, facing into the room. The
                             # sofa is exempt because layout style (b) floats it in the room.
    relations:               # (T04) used by the quality score (T09) and the generator (T11)
      sofa_tv_distance: [1.5, 3.5]    # sofa and TV unit face each other; measured front face
                                      # to front face. A 3.0 m deep room leaves about 1.7 m.
      coffee_table_gap: [0.35, 0.50]  # between sofa and TV; gap from the sofa's front face
      side_table_max_gap: 0.15        # gap to the nearer end (short side) of the sofa
      armchair_max_gap: 1.2           # gap between the armchair's and the coffee table's
                                      # footprints; the armchair stands at 90 degrees to the sofa
configs.catalog.yaml:
# Furniture catalog (Tech Spec Section 2.1).
#
# All sizes and prices are illustrative placeholders chosen by us (assumption), not retail
# data. Sizes are in meters: w = width along the front face, d = depth from front to back,
# h = height. Prices are in INR. The first variant of a slot is its default.
#
# Slots are listed in layout-vector order: `slot` must equal the entry's position, and
# reordering slots changes the meaning of every dataset built from this file.
#
# Per-slot flags (Tech Spec Sections 1 and 3.3):
#   mandatory     always present (the sofa and the TV unit in a living room)
#   rot_symmetry  1 = has a distinct front; 2 = looks the same after 180 degrees;
#                 4 = looks the same after any 90 degrees
#   needs_access  false for items that are viewed rather than walked up to (skipped by H4)
#
# `groups` lists interchangeable slots (swapping them must not change the layout). The
# living room has none; the bedroom nightstands will form one when the bedroom (P2) is added.

living_room:
  slots:
    - slot: 0
      name: sofa
      mandatory: true
      rot_symmetry: 1
      needs_access: true
      variants:
        - {id: sofa_3seater, w: 2.10, d: 0.90, h: 0.85, price: 28000}
        - {id: sofa_2seater, w: 1.60, d: 0.90, h: 0.85, price: 19000}
    - slot: 1
      name: tv_unit
      mandatory: true
      rot_symmetry: 1
      needs_access: false  # floor-standing, placed against a wall, viewed from a distance
      variants:
        - {id: tv_unit_standard, w: 1.50, d: 0.40, h: 0.50, price: 9000}
        - {id: tv_unit_large, w: 1.80, d: 0.40, h: 0.50, price: 12000}
    - slot: 2
      name: coffee_table
      mandatory: false
      rot_symmetry: 2
      needs_access: true
      variants:
        - {id: coffee_table_standard, w: 1.00, d: 0.55, h: 0.45, price: 6000}
    - slot: 3
      name: bookshelf
      mandatory: false
      rot_symmetry: 1
      needs_access: true
      variants:
        - {id: bookshelf_standard, w: 0.80, d: 0.30, h: 1.80, price: 7000}
    - slot: 4
      name: armchair
      mandatory: false
      rot_symmetry: 1
      needs_access: true
      variants:
        - {id: armchair_standard, w: 0.80, d: 0.80, h: 0.85, price: 8000}
    - slot: 5
      name: side_table
      mandatory: false
      rot_symmetry: 4
      needs_access: true
      variants:
        - {id: side_table_standard, w: 0.45, d: 0.45, h: 0.50, price: 2500}
  groups: []
